en.question: Which characteristic most clearly distinguishes an agent from a workflow?

options.text: An agent calls tools during execution, whereas a workflow does not.
options.note: Workflows commonly call tools at fixed steps, so this is not the distinction.

options.text: An agent runs asynchronously, whereas a workflow runs synchronously.
options.note: Either architecture can be implemented in either execution style.

options.text: An agent requires a larger model tier than a workflow does.
options.note: Both patterns run on whatever tier the task requires.

options.text: An agent chooses its own steps; a workflow follows a predefined path.

en.explanation: The dividing line is control of the path. A workflow has its sequence encoded by the developer; an agent decides the next action in a loop and judges when the goal is met. Tools, model size, and concurrency are orthogonal.
